content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The image has pixel rulers along its top and left edges (x increases to the right, y increases downward, 0 at the image's top-left corner). Using the ruler scale, give the position of a point inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: (x, y)

The image shows an axial slice with the patient apparently lying in an unusual orientation. There are two heterogeneous bright regions in the soft tissue. One is at the upper anterior abdominal wall (around x 230–430, y 110–250). The other is on the right of the image (around x 555–680, y 380–530).

A fibrous tumor such as a desmoid would likely appear as a heterogeneous mass within the abdominal wall. The anterior mass is larger and has a streaky, heterogeneous texture with dark strands, which fits a fibrous tumor. The lateral lesion on the right, with a dark central flow-void-like area, is also heterogeneous.

I'm choosing the anterior mass, whose centre is around (330, 175).

ANSWER: (330, 175)
